investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists anywhere in the 6-node cluster. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote agent pods or other workloads, leaving zero capacity for new pods. Supported by all three check messages reporting 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on exactly 2 nodes.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the 4 remaining nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector rules, meaning even if kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity were added to those nodes it would not help without a matching label or taint change. Supported by '4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' in failed-check.message.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioned for concurrent eval load: three separate eval probes (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran within a ~7-minute window and all hit the same exhaustion, suggesting the cluster's steady-state capacity is insufficient to absorb even observability probe traffic on top of existing workloads.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-17T18:40–18:45Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes have Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With zero viable nodes and no preemption victims available, every new remote-agent pod is stuck Unschedulable. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1905: createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)) never receives a running agent, so the probe times out and returns no evidence, causing the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, readyState, and state to be entirely unmet.

Concurrent or leaked remote-agent pods consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user workloads did not clean up remote-agent pods, the VM resource slots on the two eligible nodes may be held by existing pods, leaving none for new scheduling attempts.

No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the agent pod never left the pending state.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that are eligible to schedule remote agent pods. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists anywhere in the 6-node cluster. Because the pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) could not return any evidence, causing a total contract gap for all four required fields. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint, not a confirmed user-facing outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-17 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting 0/6 nodes available due to exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm resources on 2 eligible nodes and mismatched node affinity/selectors on the remaining 4. investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. With no schedulable node available and preemption unable to free capacity, every remote agent pod submitted by the eval runner was stuck Unschedulable for ~141–146 seconds before the check timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure, not an application code defect. No evidence of a user-facing incident or live traffic impact is present in the supplied packet; this is an eval-detected availability signal.
